dimensions.assessment: Affects plaintiffs, defendants, and legal practitioners involved in civil lawsuits seeking between $75,000 and $150,000 in diversity cases.
dimensions.evidence: raises the minimum amount in controversy from $75,000 to $150,000

dimensions.assessment: Changes the judicial forum where certain medium-value civil disputes must be brought.
dimensions.evidence: raises the minimum amount in controversy from $75,000 to $150,000 and adjusts the amount for inflation every 10 years beginning in 2030

dimensions.assessment: Direct federal spending impacts are not detailed, though shifting caseloads may affect federal court operational burdens.
Amends Title 28 of the United States Code regarding federal court jurisdiction thresholds and administrative procedures.
dimensions.evidence: To amend title 28, United States Code, to adjust thresholds relating to jurisdiction for inflation.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent change with automatic decennial inflation adjustments starting in 2030.
dimensions.evidence: Effective on January 1, 2030, and January 1 of each tenth year thereafter

missing_information: Exact count or percentage of civil cases currently filed in federal court affected by the new threshold
importance_detail.rationale: The bill modifies the financial threshold for federal court diversity jurisdiction, shifting certain civil cases out of federal courts and tying future updates to inflation.
